messages.subject: Re: Problems with Corine Land Cover Data in Wallace
messages.subject_clean: Problems with Corine Land Cover Data in Wallace
messages.body_plain:
Hi Beni,
It looks like the problem is with a conflict in the coordinate reference system of the land cover data you are using. Wallace typically uses WGS 84.
I'll take a look into if this is the problem. In the meantime you can try reprojecting your rasters into WGS84 and see if that works.

messages.subject: Threshold value selection in session code.
messages.subject_clean: Threshold value selection in session code.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wallace Team! I hope this email finds you well.

I'm currently running a full niche modeling analysis through Wallace's shiny. When I get to the Visualize module, I choose to make a prediction map using the 10 percentile training presence as a thresholding rule, and I finish the workflow by downloading the documented code.

My goal is to share the code so that other people can review and reproduce it. When I reviewed the "Visualization" section of the code to get the binary prediction map, I found the following statement "Generate a map of the Maxent generated model with a p10 threshold rule of 0.385493114590645". Where does this threshold value come from?  I have reviewed the code in previous steps, and it doesn't document exactly how Wallace obtained this value. Therefore, if there is no line in the code that tells me how to obtain this threshold value, then the code that I'm generating isn't completely reproducible.

If I'm using the 10 percentile training presence as a thresholding rule, What command or line of code can I add to get the exact threshold value to generate the binary map prediction?

Thanks for your time and help.

Best, Jhan

messages.subject: Re: Can't find the LQHPT option
messages.body_plain:
Hi, thanks for asking.
As of now, Wallace only includes Linear (L), Quadratic (Q), Product (P), Hinge (H), and combinations of those feature classes, for Maxent modeling. Otherwise, you can use ENMeval outside of Wallace to run a LQHPT model. Check out the ENMeval vignette <https://jamiemkass.github.io/ENMeval/articles/ENMeval-2.0.0-vignette.html> and this article on MaxEnt <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1600-0587.2013.07872.x> for more info.

> Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Threshold value selection in session code.
messages.subject_clean: Threshold value selection in session code.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jhan,
Thanks for bringing this to our attention. One of our team members is now fixing the session code to make it more intuitive.

In the meantime, I have some suggestions for a workaround. One is to use Wallace v1.1, in which the session code explicitly gives steps to determining the threshold value. The other option is to continue using v1.9, but you can add the following lines of code to the session code to determine the value of the threshold and how to change it if you want to.

Add the following to the chunk below where it says "### Visualize Generate a map of the maxnet generated model with with a “p10” threshold
rule of ...... " You will need to change the 'XX' to the letters used for your species.

## change Maxent to Maxnet
predSel_XX <- predictMaxnet(m_XX, bgMask_XX,
                                   type = "cloglog",
                                   clamp = TRUE)
occPredVals <- raster::extract(predSel_XX, occs_XX[ , c("longitude", "latitude")])

#select a threshold
tenpct <-quantile(occPredVals, probs = 0.1) #10pct
mtp <- quantile(occPredVals, probs = 0.0) #mtp

# Applied selected threshold
predSel_thr <- predSel_Hc > tenpct
plot(predSel_thr)

I hope that helps, and again, thank you for bringing this to our attention.
-Bethany, The Wallace team

messages.subject: Issues with MESS plotting through ggplot2
messages.subject_clean: Issues with MESS plotting through ggplot2
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wallace Team!

I'm running the model of a species that has a cis-andean distribution. My goal is to project this model in trans-andean areas. Therefore, I run MESS to find out the areas that are climatically different from the areas associated with occs. My goal is to get the MESS prediction map to use in a manuscript. However,  Wallace generates the MESS map through the leaflet library, which doesn't allow to download of the plot in PDF. To solve this problem, I have generated a code using ggplot2. However, I have encountered some issues:

1) Even though I use the same object to generate the map, the plot created with ggplot2 (MESS_ggplot2.jpg) is not the same as the generated with leaflet (MESS_leaflet.jpg). The prediction intensities are not the same, so it is unreliable.
2) When I add the MESS prediction with geom_raster, I must use "fill = as.factor (mess)", because if I don't get the following error: Continuous value supplied to discrete scale. Due to the mess variable is being read as a factor, the plot legend is too long (Legend_labels.jpg).

Also, I have reviewed the ENMeval vignette that also talks about MESS, but the ENMeval way doesn't use the background as it does the Wallace workflow. I'm only trying to find the simplest way to plot the MESS map using ggplot2 so that it is the same map generated with the leaflet library. Any help or recommendation? I attach the code (MESS_Wallace.Rmd) that I'm using to generate the MESS plot.

Best, and I wish you a merry Christmas.
Jhan.

Is your desired end result to get the MESS map as a pdf? If that's the case, I'd download it as a PNG (which is an available option through the Wallace GUI) and then export that to a pdf.
If there is another reason you are using ggplot2, I can put you in touch with someone from the team who knows a bit more about leaflet and ggplot when they are back from winter break.
Happy holidays.

-Bethany
